clue.text: Traveller from afar is missing tiresome stranger

indicators.note: stranger, as in more strange, tells us to rework the remaining letters into an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written, the pool of letters
taken as written; these letters are the ones missing from the pool

explanation.surface: A traveller from far away is missing an annoying stranger he met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is missing' says take I and S out of TIRESOME, leaving TREOME, which 'stranger' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star is a body that travels to Earth from deep space, a fair cryptic description.

clue.text: See notice in port as something alarming

parts.note: clock is slang for see or notice

indicators.note: in places the advertisement inside the name of the Brazilian port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
an ad or advert is a notice

explanation.surface: Spotting a notice in a harbour that warns of something alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedside radio with an alarm built in is literally something that sounds an alarm.

clue.text: Rubbish about female cats

indicators.note: about means going round, so rubbish wraps around the female pronoun

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: Dismissing as rubbish some tale about female cats.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTS is British slang for something worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopards and jaguars are big cats, and the word names them collectively.

clue.text: Light on vehicle must be wired

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

explanation.surface: A lamp mounted on a car has to be wired up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabled is a past-tense synonym for wired, as of a telegram sent by cable.

clue.text: Barbie may need this drawing

definitions.meaning: a barbie is Australian slang for a barbecue, which burns lumps of fuel
an artwork done with a stick of burnt wood

explanation.definitionFit: The fuel burnt on a barbecue is the same material artists use for sketching.

clue.text: Outskirts of Boulogne seen en route, comme il faut

indicators.note: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so take the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: someone en route is coming, on the way

explanation.surface: Seen on the edges of Boulogne while travelling, all very proper and French.
explanation.walkthrough: Comme il faut is French for proper, as it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means fitting or seemly, the sense of the French phrase for proper behaviour.

clue.text: Straightforward copper behind king in court

indicators.note: in places the king and copper inside the abbreviation for court
behind puts the copper after the king in the answer

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman standing behind a king in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is plain and simple, sharply defined like something straightforward.

clue.text: Heart of gold in church

indicators.note: in puts the heraldic gold inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A heart of gold kept inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of gold' reads as a phrase, but 'Heart' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The core of something is its centre or heart.

clue.text: Kid heard in river

indicators.note: heard means a word that sounds like the one given

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child heard playing in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb meaning tease. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river flowing through north-east England to the North Sea.

clue.text: New order for Carnegie — mine is old order

indicators.note: a new order for the letters of the two words means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Andrew Carnegie's mine gets new management, ending the old way of running things.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the political system of France before the 1789 Revolution, the former order of things.

clue.text: Briton released without punishment

parts.note: a Scot is a Briton
released means set free

explanation.surface: A Briton set free with no punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is an idiom meaning to escape any penalty.

clue.text: Letters from America? Read about mutual trust and friendship

indicators.note: about means stirred around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reading Letters from America, the radio talks, about trust and friendship between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters from America was a long-running BBC radio talk by Alistair Cooke; here 'Letters from' just says the answer is made from the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is the comradeship and mutual trust among friends.

clue.text: We add odd number — that may impede us

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
eight is a number

explanation.surface: We add an odd number, which only slows us down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd number' looks like a single phrase, but 'odd' rearranges WE ADD and 'number' is EIGHT, an even one.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy, inert load is a burden that hampers movement.

clue.text: Sort of Grecian urn originally found in bombed town

indicators.note: a sort of something is a rough version of it, so the letters are rearranged
originally means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A kind of Grecian urn found in a bombed town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Basque town was bombed in 1937, and Picasso's painting is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Basque town bombed during the Spanish Civil War, subject of Picasso's painting.

clue.text: Numbers of patients seen at first to be unnecessary

parts.note: needles numb patients, so they are numbers, things that numb

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The number of patients seen first makes it all pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' reads as quantities but means things that numb, pronounced NUM-ers.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not required, a direct synonym for unnecessary.

clue.text: Is a name recollected? Yes, but not with this

definitions.text: Is a name recollected? Yes, but not with this

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means gathered again in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a name is remembered, and the answer is no if you have this.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory means a person cannot recall names, which is the condition described.

clue.text: Distinguished actor's first in TV role

indicators.note: in places the actor's initial inside the television and role

parts.note: a TV is a television set
a part is a role

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: An actor first gets noticed in a TV role.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set apart is to be marked out as different, distinguished from others.

clue.text: Row D is situated next to E

parts.note: put means placed or situated

explanation.surface: Row D in a theatre sits next to row E.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line of seats, but it is the definition, a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is an argument or quarrel.

clue.text: Very fair clue — word too obscure?

indicators.note: obscure means muddled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver protests that the clue is fair, but one word is too obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tow is flax fibre, so tow-coloured hair is very fair or flaxen.

clue.text: Life in Paris one rejected — getting stuck in airport, too

indicators.note: getting stuck in places the shortened French word inside the airport

parts.note: Orly is a Paris airport

indicators.note: rejected means the letter for one is thrown out

parts.note: vie is French for life
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Life in Paris for someone rejected means being stuck at the airport too.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I from VIE leaves VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly means excessively, the same as too in too much.

clue.text: A little costermonger's call

indicators.note: a little of the word means only part of it, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A bit of a street trader's cry.
explanation.walkthrough: A costermonger is a London street seller of fruit and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To term something is to call or name it.

clue.text: Information about head of Lakeland valley

indicators.note: about means the information goes round the letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Information about the head of a Lake District valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the Lake District in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Peters the author receives a letter from Greece …

indicators.note: receives means the author's name takes the letter inside it

parts.note: Ellis Peters was the pen name of the author of the Cadfael novels
psi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An author called Peters gets a letter from Greece and trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the printed dots, which are themselves an ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: The three dots that mark an omission or trailing off are called by this name.

clue.text: See 9
Orlando's carrying on — playfully teasing, as a rule

indicators.note: carrying means holding the other pieces inside

parts.note: the setter Orlando is speaking of himself, so his means my
taken as written
arch means playfully teasing or mischievous

explanation.surface: The setter goes on being mischievous, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on' looks like a phrase but 'on' is a piece held inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarchy is rule by a king or queen.

clue.text: Getting a half-century in some matches without fail

indicators.note: in places the half-century inside the matches

parts.note: aways are away matches, played on the opponent's ground
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A batsman getting fifty in some games every time.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-century in cricket is fifty runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at all times, without fail.
